source_title: 犯人と暮らした一週間
curator_title: 犯人と暮らした一週間
opening: A man was kidnapped and spent a week with his captor. Police stormed the location, shot the captor dead, and freed him. Afterwards concerned friends contacted him. He assured them he was fine but would never tell them what had happened that week. Why?
solution: His friends were people he knew only through online gaming. After a week offline, he logged in and they worried he had been ill. He wanted to keep his real identity separate from his online identity. Admitting he was the kidnapping victim would connect him to the identifiable incident, so he reassured them without explaining his absence.

rubric.criterion: Real week-long kidnapping ends when police kill the captor and free him.
Friends are online gaming friends, concerned by his week of absence and thinking illness; contact follows his return.
He hides the kidnapping to prevent linking his real identity with his online identity, while reassuring them he is fine.

translation_notes: Japanese names neutralized. English rendering retains online/offline ambiguity without relying on language-specific wordplay. No invented obligation to specify newspaper vs television.
